# SelectionOdds

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Stats` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public static class SelectionOdds
```

How likely one asset's exact selection was, computed from the CookBook that produced it.

## Remarks

**The Set browser could already multiply its rarity table together, and that product is an estimate.** It assumes the layers roll independently, which is true of a plain book and false of every book that uses incompatibility rules or optional layers — a rule makes a combination impossible and hands its share to the survivors, so the product understates every combination that survives. This is the figure without the assumption.

**It is rejection sampling, so the normaliser is the whole point.** The generator rolls a recipe, rolls each of its layers, and throws the entire attempt away if the recipe's rules reject it — recipe included, which is why the denominator sums over the book rather than over one recipe. So the chance of a selection is its own unconditional mass divided by the mass of everything legal:

```csharp
         w_r/W  x  P(layers)
P  =  ------------------------------------------------
       SUM over recipes of  w/W  x  P(it rolls legal)
```

With no rules anywhere the denominator is exactly 1 and this reduces to the product the browser was already showing — which is the right relationship between the two: the estimate is not a different model, it is this one with its correction dropped.

**The denominator is the only expensive part, and giving up on it costs a DIRECTION, not the answer.** Each recipe's legal mass needs a walk of its combinations, budgeted exactly as [`UniqueSpace`](Nfty.Core.Generation.UniqueSpace.md) budgets its own. Every legal mass is at most 1, so the denominator is at most 1, so dropping it can only make the figure too SMALL. An un-walkable book therefore reports the numerator as [`SpaceCertainty.AtLeast`](Nfty.Core.Generation.SpaceCertainty.md#f-atleast) — a real bound — and never the upside-down one [`SpaceCertainty`](Nfty.Core.Generation.SpaceCertainty.md) exists to have caught.

**What it is a chance OF: one roll of this CookBook.** Two things deliberately do not enter it. Unique-DNA rejection is a property of a COLLECTION being filled, not of a roll, and distorts nothing until a run approaches the book's whole space. And `generate --recipe` pins a run to one recipe without recording that anywhere in the Set, so a pinned run's assets are scored against the book's own weights; a recipe the book has SHELVED is the one case that is detectable, and it reports nothing rather than a figure the book contradicts.

## Methods

### Describe(SelectionChance, bool) { #m-describe-nfty-core-stats-selectionchance-system-boolean }

```csharp
public static string Describe(SelectionChance chance, bool asOdds);
```

Renders a chance the way every figure in this project is rendered: invariant, and saying which direction it is bounded in when it is bounded at all.

**Parameters**

- `chance` (`SelectionChance`) - The figure.
- `asOdds` (`bool`) - True for "1 in N", false for a percentage.

**Returns.** The figure, or an empty string when there is nothing to say.

**Remarks**

Worded HERE rather than in a front-end, for the reason [`SpaceText`](Nfty.Core.Generation.SpaceText.md) already records: the CLI and the GUI printing one number two ways is a defect nothing fails on. Note the direction INVERTS between the two units — a floor on the probability is a ceiling on the odds — which is exactly the kind of flip two hand-written copies get wrong in opposite ways.

### Prepare(PeekedCookBook, long) { #m-prepare-nfty-core-formats-peekedcookbook-system-int64 }

```csharp
public static BookOdds Prepare(PeekedCookBook book, long enumerationBudget = 1000000);
```

Resolves everything about a book that does not depend on which asset is being priced — the per-layer outcome probabilities and, above all, the denominator.

**Parameters**

- `book` (`PeekedCookBook`) - The book to price against. Never throws on a broken one; it simply cannot price anything.
- `enumerationBudget` (`long`) - How many combinations may be walked per recipe; see [`UniqueSpace.DefaultEnumerationBudget`](Nfty.Core.Generation.UniqueSpace.md#f-defaultenumerationbudget).

**Returns.** The prepared book.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` - The budget is zero or negative.

**Remarks**

The same split [`WeightedRoller.Prepare()`](../nfty-ticket/Nfty.Core.Generation.WeightedRoller.md#m-prepare-system-collections-generic-ireadonlydictionary-2d4b54) makes, for the same reason: the denominator is a fixed property of the book and the only part of this that can cost real time, so a caller pricing a grid of five hundred assets must not pay for it five hundred times.
